scope_summary: Imported candidate for Thermodynamics & Heat Engines. No authority is carried; every gap below must be authored before this can be admitted.

microtopics.title: Thermodynamics & Heat Engines
entry_assumptions: **First Law Sign Convention Precondition**: First Law $\Delta U = Q - W$ where $W = \int P dV$ is work done **by** the system. (Alternatively, IUPAC $\Delta U = Q + W_{\text{on}}$). Consistency in sign convention must be preserved throughout an entire derivation.

**Second Law & Carnot Efficiency Ceiling Invariant**: No heat engine operating between two thermal reservoirs at temperatures $T_H$ and $T_C$ can have an efficiency exceeding the reversible Carnot efficiency: $\eta \le \eta_{\text{Carnot}} = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Internal energy as state function: $U = \frac{f}{2} n R T$; $\Delta U$ depends only on initial and final states, not path.

teaching_path.action: Cyclic process invariant: $\oint dU = 0 \implies Q_{\text{net}} = W_{\text{net}} = \text{Area inside } P\text{-}V \text{ loop}$.
Identifying degrees of freedom $f$: monoatomic ($f=3, \gamma=5/3$), diatomic ($f=5, \gamma=7/5$).

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Saying a hot body "contains more heat" than a cold body.
misconceptions.repair: Heat ($Q$) is energy in transit across a boundary due to temperature difference. A body contains *internal energy* ($U$), never heat.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Assuming temperature remains constant in adiabatic expansion because $Q = 0$.
misconceptions.repair: In adiabatic expansion, $W > 0$ and $Q = 0$. By First Law, $\Delta U = -W < 0 \implies n C_v \Delta T < 0$. Temperature strictly drops during adiabatic expansion.
